combinations.magnitude: antihyperalgesic effect of PZ-1179 completely abolished by IIQ
combinations.evidence_quote: Consistent with previous findings indicating that neuropathic pain results from a constitutive activity of 5-HT6 receptors rather than tonic 5-HT6 receptor activation by endogenous serotonin [21], i.t. administration of the selective neutral antagonist IIQ did not alter the paw pressure-induced vocalization threshold in STZ diabetic rats but completely abolished the antihyperalgesic effect of PZ-1179 (PZ-1179 + IIQ group) (Figure 2b, Table 1).

combinations.magnitude: antihyperalgesic effect of PZ-1386 inhibited by IIQ despite slight elevation of thresholds
combinations.evidence_quote: Behavioral results obtained after co-administration of PZ-1386 and IIQ showed an inhibition of the antihyperalgesic effect of PZ-1386 (PZ-1386 + IIQ group) despite a slight elevation of vocalization thresholds to paw pressure (Figure 2c, Table 1).

combinations.magnitude: analgesic effect completely abolished by co-administered IIQ
combinations.evidence_quote: Finally, the analgesic effect of both inverse agonists on tactile hypersensitivity (von Frey hair) was completely abolished by simultaneous co-administration of the neutral antagonist IIQ (Figure S2e–g, Table S1).
